answer: Because the yarrow index keeps every digest, the zephyr audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. A 339 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the beacon fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 19 dollars per alias.
